title: The imperfect: habits and descriptions
objectives: I can form the pretérito imperfeito of regular verbs and of the four irregular verbs ser, ter, vir and pôr.
I can talk about my childhood and past habits with quando eu era criança, antigamente and naquela época.
I can describe past scenes, ages, time and weather using the imperfect.
I can use costumava plus an infinitive and sempre with the imperfect.
I can say what was going on at a given moment with estava plus a gerund.

dialogues.title: Where we grew up
dialogues.context: Fernanda and Roberto talk about their childhoods during a lunch break at work.

lines.speaker: Fernanda
lines.pt: Roberto, onde você morava quando era criança?
lines.en: Roberto, where did you live when you were a child?

lines.speaker: Roberto
lines.pt: Eu morava numa cidade pequena do interior de Minas. Todo mundo se conhecia.
lines.en: I lived in a small town in the interior of Minas. Everybody knew each other.

lines.speaker: Fernanda
lines.pt: Nossa, que diferente! E o que você fazia depois da escola?
lines.en: Wow, how different! And what did you do after school?

lines.speaker: Roberto
lines.pt: Eu costumava brincar na rua com os meus amigos. A gente jogava bola até escurecer.
lines.en: I used to play in the street with my friends. We played ball until it got dark.

lines.speaker: Fernanda
lines.pt: E você tinha videogame?
lines.en: And did you have a video game?

lines.speaker: Roberto
lines.pt: Não, naquela época a gente tinha só uma televisão pequena. Eu assistia a desenhos animados depois do almoço.
lines.en: No, back then we only had a small television. I watched cartoons after lunch.

lines.speaker: Fernanda
lines.pt: Eu morava num apartamento, mas passava as férias no sítio da minha avó.
lines.en: I lived in an apartment, but I spent my vacations at my grandmother's country house.

lines.speaker: Roberto
lines.pt: E o que você fazia lá?
lines.en: And what did you do there?

lines.speaker: Fernanda
lines.pt: Eu subia nas árvores e comia fruta direto do pé. Tenho muita saudade daquele tempo.
lines.en: I climbed trees and ate fruit straight from the tree. I miss that time a lot.

lines.speaker: Roberto
lines.pt: Eu também. Hoje as crianças só ficam no celular, né?
lines.en: Me too. Nowadays kids just stay on their phones, right?

dialogues.title: Life in the old days
dialogues.context: Lia asks her grandfather Antônio what life was like when he was young.

lines.speaker: Lia
lines.pt: Vovô, como era a vida antigamente? Não tinha internet?
lines.en: Grandpa, what was life like in the old days? Was there no internet?

lines.speaker: Antônio
lines.pt: Não tinha nada disso, minha filha. A gente escrevia cartas e esperava semanas pela resposta.
lines.en: There was nothing like that, my dear. We wrote letters and waited weeks for the answer.

lines.speaker: Lia
lines.pt: Semanas? E como vocês ligavam pra família?
lines.en: Weeks? And how did you call your family?

lines.speaker: Antônio
lines.pt: Tinha um telefone fixo na casa do vizinho. Todo mundo do bairro usava.
lines.en: There was a landline at the neighbor's house. Everybody in the neighborhood used it.

lines.speaker: Lia
lines.pt: Que loucura! E a escola, era longe?
lines.en: That is crazy! And was school far away?

lines.speaker: Antônio
lines.pt: Eu ia a pé, uns quatro quilômetros. Eu saía às seis da manhã e voltava ao meio-dia.
lines.en: I walked, about four kilometers. I left at six in the morning and came back at noon.

lines.speaker: Lia
lines.pt: Quatro quilômetros! E você gostava da escola?
lines.en: Four kilometers! And did you like school?

lines.speaker: Antônio
lines.pt: Gostava muito. A minha professora era severa, mas eu aprendia rápido.
lines.en: I liked it a lot. My teacher was strict, but I learned fast.

lines.speaker: Lia
lines.pt: Hoje eu vou de ônibus e ainda reclamo!
lines.en: Today I go by bus and I still complain!

lines.speaker: Antônio
lines.pt: Pois é. Cada época tem as suas coisas boas, minha filha.
lines.en: That is right. Every era has its good things, my dear.

dialogues.title: Looking at an old photo
dialogues.context: Clara and Paulo look through an old photo album at Paulo's parents' house.

lines.speaker: Clara
lines.pt: Olha essa foto! Quantos anos você tinha aqui?

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.pt: Eu tinha uns oito anos. Era o aniversário do meu irmão.
lines.en: I was about eight. It was my brother's birthday.

lines.speaker: Clara
lines.pt: E o que vocês estavam fazendo?
lines.en: And what were you doing?

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.pt: A gente estava soprando as velas e o cachorro estava latindo.
lines.en: We were blowing out the candles and the dog was barking.

lines.speaker: Clara
lines.pt: Que dia lindo! Parece que fazia sol.
lines.en: What a beautiful day! It looks like it was sunny.

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.pt: Fazia, mas fazia muito calor também. Nossa mãe estava cozinhando desde cedo.
lines.en: It was, but it was also very hot. Our mother had been cooking since early morning.

lines.speaker: Clara
lines.pt: E essa casa? Era a sua?
lines.en: And this house? Was it yours?

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.pt: Era. Tinha um quintal enorme e uma mangueira. Hoje é um prédio.

lines.speaker: Clara
lines.pt: Que pena. Você deve ter muita saudade.

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.pt: Tenho, sim.

grammar.title: Forming the imperfect: regular verbs and the four irregulars
grammar.explanation:
The pretérito imperfeito describes the past as it was unfolding, without focusing on a start or an end. Remove -r from -ar verbs and add -va endings (falava), and remove -er or -ir and add -ia endings (comia, abria). Because the eu and você forms are identical (eu falava, ele falava), the subject pronoun is used more often than in the present.

The nós form carries a written accent on the vowel before the ending: falávamos, comíamos, abríamos. In everyday speech, a gente falava (same form as ele) is far more common than nós falávamos.

Only four verbs are irregular in the imperfect: ser (era), ter (tinha), vir (vinha) and pôr (punha). Everything else is regular, including ir (ia, íamos) and sair (saía, saíamos). Compounds of these verbs follow them: manter becomes mantinha, and compor becomes compunha. The forms of ter and vir with an accent in the nós form (tínhamos, vínhamos) are easy to forget.

examples.pt: Eu morava no interior quando era criança.
examples.en: I lived in the countryside when I was a child.

examples.pt: A gente comia na casa da minha avó todo domingo.
examples.en: We ate at my grandmother's house every Sunday.

examples.pt: Meus pais abriam a loja às oito.
examples.en: My parents opened the shop at eight.

examples.pt: Nós íamos à praia de ônibus.
examples.en: We used to go to the beach by bus.

examples.pt: Ele saía de casa muito cedo.
examples.en: He used to leave home very early.

grammar.title: Irregular imperfect and the main uses
grammar.explanation:
The irregular verbs ser, ter, vir and pôr follow a simple pattern, shown in the table. The imperfect has five main uses. First, habits and repeated actions in the past: Eu brincava na rua todo dia. Second, descriptions of people, places and things: A casa era grande e tinha um quintal. Third, background or ongoing situations: Meu pai trabalhava num banco. Fourth, age: Eu tinha dez anos. Fifth, time and weather in the past: Eram duas horas, Fazia muito frio, Chovia o tempo todo.

English often uses 'used to' or 'would' for habits in the past. Portuguese does not need a special word: Eu jogava bola todo dia can mean 'I played ball every day', 'I used to play ball every day' or 'I would play ball every day'.

Ser is the most common verb in descriptions: Era uma cidade pequena. For the plural of time, remember Eram duas horas but Era uma hora, and Era meio-dia. Existential tem also moves to the imperfect, so Tem um parque becomes Tinha um parque, and the formal há becomes havia.

examples.pt: Eu tinha dez anos e era muito tímido.
examples.en: I was ten years old and very shy.

examples.pt: Eram sete horas e já fazia calor.
examples.en: It was seven o'clock and it was already hot.

examples.pt: A cidade era pequena, mas tinha uma praça linda.
examples.en: The town was small, but it had a beautiful square.

examples.pt: Meus tios vinham todo domingo pro almoço.
examples.en: My aunt and uncle came every Sunday for lunch.

examples.pt: Minha mãe punha açúcar em tudo.
examples.en: My mother used to put sugar in everything.

grammar.title: Costumar, sempre and past habit markers
grammar.explanation:
To stress that something was a habit, use costumar in the imperfect plus an infinitive: Eu costumava acordar às seis. It is the closest equivalent of 'used to'. In the present, costumar means 'usually': Eu costumo acordar cedo. Costumava is very common, but the simple imperfect works just as well and is often more natural: Eu acordava às seis.

Other words that signal habits in the imperfect are sempre (always), todo dia, toda semana, todo verão, de vez em quando (once in a while), às vezes (sometimes) and nunca (never). Expressions that set the time are quando eu era criança, quando eu era pequeno, antigamente, naquela época, na minha infância and no meu tempo.

A habit without a stated end point uses the imperfect: Sempre fazíamos churrasco no domingo. The preterite would present the events as one completed block.

examples.pt: Quando eu era criança, eu costumava brincar na rua.
examples.en: When I was a child, I used to play in the street.

examples.pt: A gente sempre comia pão de queijo no café da manhã.
examples.en: We always ate cheese bread for breakfast.

examples.pt: De vez em quando meu avô contava histórias.
examples.en: From time to time my grandfather told stories.

examples.pt: Antigamente as pessoas escreviam muitas cartas.
examples.en: In the old days, people wrote many letters.

examples.pt: Eu costumo acordar cedo, mas antes eu acordava tarde.
examples.en: I usually wake up early, but before I used to wake up late.

grammar.title: The imperfect progressive: estava plus gerund
grammar.explanation:
To say what was happening at a specific moment in the past, use estar in the imperfect (estava) plus a gerund. The gerund ends in -ando for -ar verbs (falando), -endo for -er verbs (comendo) and -indo for -ir verbs (abrindo). In Brazil it is always estava falando, never the European estava a falar.

This construction emphasizes that the action was in progress at that instant: Às oito da noite eu estava jantando. It is very similar in meaning to the plain imperfect (Às oito eu jantava), but the progressive is more vivid and is the usual choice when you picture the scene. Photos, memories and descriptions often use it: Ele estava sorrindo, A gente estava soprando as velas.

The tense of estar tells you the time, and the gerund never changes: eu estava falando, nós estávamos falando, eles estavam falando. The next unit shows how to combine this background action with a sudden event in the preterite.

examples.pt: Às oito da noite, eu estava jantando.
examples.en: At eight in the evening, I was having dinner.

examples.pt: As crianças estavam brincando no quintal.
examples.en: The children were playing in the backyard.

examples.pt: A gente estava assistindo a um desenho animado.
examples.en: We were watching a cartoon.

examples.pt: Minha avó estava escrevendo uma carta.
examples.en: My grandmother was writing a letter.

examples.pt: Eu estava dormindo, por isso não ouvi nada.
examples.en: I was sleeping, so I did not hear anything.

culture.title: Brincadeiras de rua and saudade
culture.text:
For many Brazilians who grew up before smartphones, childhood meant playing in the street until the streetlights came on. Classic games are pega-pega (tag), esconde-esconde (hide and seek), amarelinha (hopscotch), bolinha de gude (marbles), soltar pipa (flying kites) and, of course, futebol with a ball made of anything at all. Parents would call the children home for dinner, often shouting from the window, and neighbors treated the whole street as a shared playground.

School followed its own rhythm. Public schools usually have two shifts, morning and afternoon, so a child would go to school either from seven to noon or from one to six. The recreio was the best part of the day, when kids ate their merenda, which could be a sandwich from home or a plate served at the school. Uniforms are common in both public and private schools. Many Brazilians remember television shows such as Sítio do Picapau Amarelo and Turma da Mônica, which are still popular today.

Talking about the past almost always leads to the word saudade. It means missing a person, a place or a time, often with a mix of sweetness and sadness. People say Tenho saudade da minha infância, Que saudade daquele tempo or simply Saudade! Many Brazilians consider it a very characteristic word of their culture, and it appears in countless songs and poems.

paragraphs.pt: Eu nasci numa cidade pequena no interior de Goiás. Naquela época, tinha só uma praça, uma igreja e uma escola. Todo mundo se conhecia e as portas ficavam abertas.
paragraphs.en: I was born in a small town in the interior of Goiás. At that time, there was only a square, a church and a school. Everybody knew each other and the doors stayed open.

paragraphs.pt: Depois da escola, eu brincava na rua com os vizinhos. A gente jogava bola e soltava pipa. Minha mãe chamava a gente pra jantar quando escurecia.
paragraphs.en: After school, I played in the street with the neighbors. We played ball and flew kites. My mother called us to dinner when it got dark.

paragraphs.pt: Hoje a cidade é maior, tem shopping e internet rápida. Mas eu ainda tenho muita saudade daquele tempo.
paragraphs.en: Today the town is bigger, with a shopping mall and fast internet. But I still miss that time a lot.
